title: The geometric viewpoint: tensors on Minkowski spacetime
summary: Lorentz transformations as isometries of the interval; 4-vectors by transformation law, bases and coordinate bases, the metric as inner product; one-forms, the gradient, raising and lowering; (M,N) tensors as multilinear maps, contraction, invariant tensors; 4-velocity, 4-momentum, 4-acceleration and the number-flux 4-vector with its conservation law. Flat spacetime throughout.

objectives.description: State the transformation laws of vectors, one-forms and (M,N) tensors under Lorentz transformations and prove that contraction of an upper with a lower index yields a tensor while summing two upper indices does not.
Derive the components and invariants of the 4-velocity, 4-momentum and 4-acceleration, including u·a = 0 and the interpretation of a·a as the squared proper acceleration.
Integrate the worldline of constant proper acceleration and check its Newtonian limit and units.
Decide whether a given object is a tensor, naming the class of transformations under which the claim holds.

preparation.description: Read the Lecture Guide's synopses of Lectures 1–3 (PDF page 1): Lorentz transformations and the displacement 4-vector, component notation, basis vectors and the metric; coordinate bases, 4-velocity, 4-momentum, 4-acceleration, (M,N) tensors, raising and lowering, number flux; contraction and the dual nature of vectors.
Watch Lecture 1: Introduction and the Geometric Viewpoint on Physics (transcript available on the page).
Watch Lecture 2: Introduction to Tensors (transcript available).
Watch or read the transcript of Lecture 3: Tensors Continued (contraction, 1-forms).
Second account: Tong, General Relativity, Section 1.2.1 A Particle in Minkowski Spacetime (within Section 1.2; reference-only; same signature).
Optional second account: Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, Chapter 1 Special Relativity and Flat Spacetime (reference-only).

activities.title: Lecture: tensors on Minkowski spacetime
activities.instructions: Read the lesson after watching Lectures 1–2. Reproduce the derivations of u·u = −1 and u·a = 0 without notes. Write out the transformation law of a (1,2) tensor in full once; it is the last time you will need to.

activities.title: Tutorial: hyperbolic motion; tensor or not?
activities.instructions: Attempt exercise 1 before asking for any hint; carry c through the final part. Then attempt exercise 2, writing the transformation class for every tensor claim. Submit each attempt when you believe it is complete; revise after feedback.

activities.title: Explain: why multilinear maps
activities.instructions: Write exercise 3 without the notes open.

activities.title: Retrieval: definitions of the unit
activities.instructions: From memory: the defining property of a Lorentz transformation; the transformation laws for upper and lower indices; the definition of an (M,N) tensor; u^μ, p^μ and their invariants; the number-flux conservation law.

exitCheck.description: Exercise 1 accepted: u·a = 0 and a·a = α² derived, the hyperbolic worldline integrated with its Newtonian limit and the c-restored form, units checked.

commonMisconceptions.claim: Any quantity with four components is a 4-vector.
commonMisconceptions.correction: A 4-vector is defined by its transformation law A′^μ = Λ^μ_ν A^ν. (E, p) qualifies because p^μ = m dx^μ/dτ; (t, |x|) does not.

commonMisconceptions.claim: The inner product of two 4-vectors is Σ_μ A^μ B^μ.
commonMisconceptions.correction: It is η_μν A^μ B^ν = −A⁰B⁰ + A·B in our convention; the plain sum of products is not Lorentz invariant (exercise 2 shows the analogous failure for Σ T^μμ).

commonMisconceptions.claim: The 4-acceleration points along the 4-velocity, like Newtonian acceleration along velocity in rectilinear motion.
commonMisconceptions.correction: u·a = 0 always: a is spacelike and Minkowski-orthogonal to u, with a·a equal to the squared proper acceleration.

commonMisconceptions.claim: Partial derivatives of tensor components are always tensors.
commonMisconceptions.correction: Only under transformations with constant Λ (inertial coordinates). In curvilinear coordinates, or under general coordinate changes, ∂_μ A_ν is not a tensor; the covariant derivative of unit 2 repairs this. The antisymmetric part ∂_μ A_ν − ∂_ν A_μ is a tensor in general (exercise 2).

checks.name: mathematical-review
checks.evidence: Build agent re-derived: Λᵀ η Λ = η from interval invariance; inverse transformation of basis vectors and one-form components; contraction via Λ Λ⁻¹ = 1; u^μ = γ(1, v) with u·u = −1; p·p = −m² and E² = p² + m²; u·a = 0 and a·a = α² in the rest frame; the continuity equation from ∂_μ N^μ = 0; for exercise 1, u = (cosh ατ, sinh ατ), t = sinh(ατ)/α, x = (cosh(ατ) − 1)/α, (x + 1/α)² − t² = 1/α², v = tanh ατ, x ≈ ½αt² for ατ ≪ 1; for exercise 2, the boost counterexample Σ T^μμ = γ²(1 + v²) versus η_μν T^μν = −1 for T = u u, and the cancellation of the second-derivative terms in ∂_μ A_ν − ∂_ν A_μ under general coordinate changes.
